established.yearText: Rebuilt by Tirumala Nayak and predecessors

heroImage.alt: Gopuram of the Meenakshi Amman Temple, Madurai

paragraphs: The Meenakshi Amman Temple (Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple) in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, is a historic temple dedicated to the goddess Meenakshi, a form of Parvati, and her consort Sundareswarar, a form of Shiva. Unusually among major Hindu temples, the goddess is the principal deity and is worshipped first.

The temple's fourteen gopurams, sculpted Hall of a Thousand Pillars, and the annual Meenakshi Thirukalyanam (celestial wedding) festival during Chithirai make it one of the most visited temples in India and the heart of the ancient city of Madurai.

festivals.name: Chithirai Thiruvizha (Meenakshi Thirukalyanam)
festivals.description: The celestial wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, drawing over a million pilgrims.

festivals.name: Navaratri
festivals.description: Golu displays and special abhishekams for the goddess.

visitingInfo.bestTime: October to March; Chithirai (Apr–May) for the wedding festival
visitingInfo.dressCode: Traditional attire; strict dress code enforced

howToReach.road: Well connected by NH roads and buses
